anomalies.observed: In the 'Main Pump & Valve Drivers' sheet the ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch is drawn as an AO3400A (small SOT-23 N-MOSFET, T6), while the AON6407 8-DFN N-MOSFET named by the spec for that position instead appears as T1 in the 24 V input path ('Reverse polarity protection'). The two N-channel devices are effectively swapped between the two positions.
anomalies.expected: Specification §2 states the ATO valve switch is 'T3 — AON6407 (8-DFN N-MOSFET) | ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch', i.e. the large AON6407 should sit at the ATO valve, not a small AO3400A.

evidence.quote: Main Pump & Valve Drivers sheet, ATO Valve block: 'T6 AO3400A'; Power Train block: 'T1 AON6407' (reverse polarity protection)
T3 — AON6407 (8-DFN N-MOSFET) | ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch

anomalies.impact: The ATO valve is switched by a different, much smaller device than intended (lower current/thermal margin, different footprint), and the 24 V input path uses a device not described in the intended design, so the built board does not match the intended actuator drive.

anomalies.observed: The 'WATER LEVEL SENSOR/SWITCHES' sheet contains a LiDAR module (PR4, 'LiDAR', PB_1.25mm) whose SCL/SDA/VCC/GND are wired out through H11 and tied to the main I2C bus (NET0025 / NET0055). This is the water-height sensing block.
anomalies.expected: Specification §4.3/§6 states the TF-Luna LiDAR (PR1) is present in the BOM but 'its pins are typed free', 'on_board: no', i.e. it 'is not connected to any net in this design'; water level in the intended design is sensed by an HC-SR04-style ultrasonic sensor on two GPIOs, not by a wired LiDAR.

evidence.quote: Water Level Sensor/Switches sheet, Water Height Sensor block: 'PR4 LiDAR', 'H11 PB_1.25mm', 'C53 100u', labels NET0025 / NET0055
the r2 netlist shows PR1 with on_board: no, in_bom: yes, and all four pins (VCC, SDA, SCL, GND) typed free — i.e., it is not connected to any net in this design

anomalies.impact: The LiDAR interface is actually wired in this build (contradicting the intended design in which it is documentation-only), so the board's water-level interface differs from the specified one.

parsed.summary: The drawing is largely consistent with the specification, but two deviations are visible: the ATO-valve MOSFET is an AO3400A rather than the specified AON6407 (the AON6407 being used instead at T1 in the 24 V input path), and the water-level block wires a LiDAR module to the I2C bus even though the intended design leaves the TF-Luna unwired.
